The real value of multiple models might just be their disagreements. 
Today, while revisiting the multi-model private chat for @OpenGradient , I suddenly lost interest in arguing about 'which model is the strongest.' What's truly useful is to hand the same trading plan to different models and see where they diverge. 
When using AI for research, my biggest fear isn’t when it directly says 'I don’t know,' but rather when it presents a very complete answer that only follows a one-sided logic. If you only look at one model, smoothness can easily be mistaken for correctness. #ETH 
OpenGradient Chat puts multiple models into a single private AI portal, chat.opengradient.ai. For me, this shouldn't just be a list of more model names; it should be a way to 'let the answers find each other’s flaws.' 
For example, when analyzing the same token, one model might prioritize product growth, while another might first highlight unlocks, liquidity, and data biases. When they provide different conclusions, I don’t rush to pick the one that seems 'more correct'; instead, I first clarify whether the discrepancies arise from different facts or different judgment criteria. The parts we agree on give me confidence, while the disagreements remind me to check my assumptions. #BTC 
The privacy aspect is also crucial. If I need to compare answers, I have to replicate my position logic, wallet habits, and undisclosed plans across several platforms. The more I compare, the larger my exposure becomes. Multiple models should only be paired with private access so that it’s not just stacking menus. 
This is also my new standard when looking at product lines like $OPG : the number of models isn’t the most important thing. What matters is whether users can expose unseen risks using multiple answers without increasing privacy risks; that’s closer to true utility. 
So today I’m left with one question: if several models provide different conclusions, can OpenGradient Chat help users see exactly where they diverged? 
@OpenGradient  $OPG  #OPG

欧洲从封建王权到议会政治，美国从建国到民权运动，本质上都经历过无数次关于权力边界和资源分配权的争论。
